trial_court: I Additional Judge to the Court of District Judge, Indore in Civil Misc. Case No. 10/86
facts_of_case: NA/husband instituted petition under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage by decree of divorce. Case was registered as Hindu Marriage Case No. 223/84. Ex-parte decree dissolving the marriage was passed on 3-5-1985.

legal_principles.principle: The provisions under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code are required to be construed liberally.
legal_principles.held: Normally, the parties should be deprived of the opportunity of hearing only in case of gross negligence and mis-conduct.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order 9 Rule 13

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside an ex-parte decree to show sufficient cause.
legal_principles.held: It is also not clear as to why the Court proceeded to hear the matter without serious endeavour to bring about reconciliation.

legal_principles.principle: A finding of fact is not liable to be dislodged or demolished unless it is shown that the Court has acted in gross error.
legal_principles.held: This conclusion is no firm foundation and is not liable to be dislodged or demolished.
cited_cases: AIR 1986 SC 509—Dudh Nath Pandey v. Suresh Chandra Bhatta Sali

outcome.final_order: Application for setting aside ex-parte decree and condonation of delay in initiating proceedings was dismissed by trial court.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act
arguing sufficient cause for absence in a family court
seeking ex-parte decree in a civil procedure case
